t.1.70.1: To him who spoke thus, Janaka, with joined palms, replied: "May good fortune be yours; you should hear our lineage, which is celebrated as most excellent. For at the giving of a daughter in marriage, O best of sages, one born of a noble family must recount his lineage in full; learn it, O great sage."
t.1.70.2: There was a king, Nimi, renowned throughout the three worlds by his own deeds, supremely righteous in spirit and the foremost of all who possess strength of character.
t.1.70.3: His son was named Mithi, and Mithi's son was Janaka, the first to bear the name Janaka; and from Janaka, in turn, came Udāvasu.
t.1.70.4: From Udāvasu was born the righteous-souled Nandivardhana, and the son of Nandivardhana was named Suketu.
t.1.70.5: From Suketu, too, was born the righteous and mighty Devarāta; and of the royal sage Devarāta, the son was renowned as Bṛhadratha.
t.1.70.7: From Sudhṛti was born the righteous-souled and most virtuous Dhṛṣṭaketu, and from the royal sage Dhṛṣṭaketu came the one renowned as Haryaśva.
t.1.70.6: To Bṛhadratha was born the heroic and valiant Mahāvīra; to Mahāvīra was born the steadfast Sudhṛti, whose prowess was true.
t.1.70.8: Haryaśva's son was Maru, and Maru's son was Pratīndhaka. The son of Pratīndhaka was the righteous-souled king Kīrtiratha.
t.1.70.9: The son of Kīrtiratha, too, is remembered as Devamīḍha; Devamīḍha's son was Vibudha, and Vibudha's son was Mahīdhraka.
t.1.70.10: The son of Mahīdhraka was King Kīrtirāta, of great strength. To Kīrtirāta, that royal sage, Mahāromā was born.
t.1.70.11: From Mahāromā was born the righteous Svarṇaromā, and from Svarṇaromā, the royal sage, was born Hrasvaromā.
t.1.70.12: To that great-souled knower of dharma two sons were born: I am the elder, and my younger brother is the heroic Kuśadhvaja.
t.1.70.13: But that lord of men, my father, consecrated me, the eldest, in the kingship, and having placed the burden of Kuśadhvaja upon me, he departed for the forest.
t.1.70.14: When our aged father had gone to heaven, I looked with affection upon my godlike brother Kuśadhvaja, who righteously bore the burden of rule.
t.1.70.15: Then, after some time had passed, the mighty king Sudhanvā came from the city of Sāṃkāśya to Mithilā, intent on laying siege to it.
t.1.70.16: And he sent word to me, saying, “Let the peerless bow of Śiva and the lotus-eyed maiden Sītā be given to me.”
t.1.70.17: Because I would not give her to him, O brahmarṣi, there was war between him and me; and that king Sudhanvā, facing me head-on, was slain by me in battle.
t.1.70.18: Having slain that king Sudhanvan, O best of sages, I consecrated my heroic brother Kuśadhvaja as king in Sāṃkāśya.
t.1.70.19: This is my younger brother, and I am the elder, O great sage. Supremely delighted, I give the two brides to you, O bull among sages.
t.1.70.20: Sītā to Rāma, may good fortune be yours, and Ūrmilā to Lakṣmaṇa: my daughter Sītā, whose bride-price was valor, who is like a daughter of the gods.
t.1.70.21: And the second, Ūrmilā, as well, I say it three times, there is no doubt: supremely pleased, I give these two as brides, O Raghunandana.
t.1.70.22: O king, have the godāna ceremony performed for Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, and the rite for the ancestors as well; may good fortune be yours. Then carry out the wedding ceremony.
t.1.70.23: Today, O mighty-armed one, is Maghā; on the third day, O lord, under the constellation Uttara Phalgunī, O king, perform the wedding rite. For the sake of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, a gift that gives rise to happiness should be made.
